title: The RTL8922 Spectrum Spectacular
browser_recording_note: Optional passive UI footage, no new RF stimulus; no counters removed. Offline render uses still fallback.
audio: Original procedural bass music, airhorns and hitmarkers; expressive neural synthetic actor.

voiceover.speaker: Ryan
voiceover.delivery_instruction: Speak English as an outrageously enthusiastic American used car salesman hosting a ridiculous gaming montage. A warm, natural, smiling male voice. Very expressive, playful and excited, with big pitch changes, punchy emphasis, comic pauses and a slightly breathless sales pitch. Really sell the punchlines. Sound like a lively human actor, not a robot or a calm audiobook narrator. Keep every word clear. No background music.

clips.text: Oh, BABY! Is your Wi-Fi card just... doing Wi-Fi? Folks, that is a TRAGEDY! Welcome to the Spectrum Spectacular!
ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY MILLION complex samples a second! That's right! This baby has more bandwidth than my entire personality!
Look at that waterfall! Two hundred and forty FFTs a second! The spectrum is absolutely COOKING!
One hundred and sixty megahertz! Eight slices! Eight valid header checksums! EIGHT FOR EIGHT! Somebody clip that!
Four hundred forty-one bytes! Decoded in software! Matching frame checksum! Oh my goodness, the checksums CHECK OUT!
But WAIT! There's MORE! Two point four! Five! Six gigahertz! Every band must go! Sequentially, of course. We're ridiculous, not magical!
Overflow? Skill issue! Just kidding. We mark the gap, reload, and get right back in the game! THAT'S the comeback! Tune while streaming!
The RTL eighty-nine twenty-two SDR! Open source! Experimental! Deal with the BANDWIDTH! Some debugging required. Imaginary warranties sold separately!

timeline.title: MOM! GET THE ANTENNA!
timeline.narration: Oh, BABY! Is your Wi-Fi card just... doing Wi-Fi? Folks, that is a TRAGEDY! Welcome to the Spectrum Spectacular!
timeline.qualification: Actual RTL8922AE receive experiments. Dealership enthusiasm sold separately.

timeline.narration: ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY MILLION complex samples a second! That's right! This baby has more bandwidth than my entire personality!
timeline.qualification: Experimental PAXI RX. 80 / 160 MS/s passed bounded 60-second application trials.

timeline.title: LOOK AT THAT WATERFALL.
timeline.narration: Look at that waterfall! Two hundred and forty FFTs a second! The spectrum is absolutely COOKING!
timeline.qualification: 240 FFT/s target; screen refresh limits redraws. Recorded passive RX; Pluto TX off.

timeline.title: ONE BURST. ALL 160 MHz.
timeline.narration: One hundred and sixty megahertz! Eight slices! Eight valid header checksums! EIGHT FOR EIGHT! Somebody clip that!
timeline.qualification: Same HE-SU PHY header in eight 20 MHz sections. Two-stream payload not decoded.

timeline.title: THE CHECKSUMS CHECK OUT.
timeline.narration: Four hundred forty-one bytes! Decoded in software! Matching frame checksum! Oh my goodness, the checksums CHECK OUT!
timeline.qualification: Legacy 20 MHz OFDM extracted from 160 MS/s I/Q. Independent FCS: a232c556.

timeline.title: BUT WAIT! THERE'S MORE!
timeline.narration: But WAIT! There's MORE! Two point four! Five! Six gigahertz! Every band must go! Sequentially, of course. We're ridiculous, not magical!
timeline.qualification: Sequentially stitched survey, not simultaneous full-band RX. Above 6 GHz RF unqualified.

timeline.title: OVERFLOW? GET BACK UP.
timeline.narration: Overflow? Skill issue! Just kidding. We mark the gap, reload, and get right back in the game! THAT'S the comeback! Tune while streaming!
timeline.qualification: Retunes mark brief gaps without reload. Fault recovery reloads the isolated driver.

timeline.title: RTL8922 SDR
timeline.narration: The RTL eighty-nine twenty-two SDR! Open source! Experimental! Deal with the BANDWIDTH! Some debugging required. Imaginary warranties sold separately!
timeline.qualification: One receive path. Firmware held. Indefinite continuity, full-band EVM / sensitivity unqualified.
